sections.content: When most investors think of Texas real estate, they picture Austin, Dallas, or Houston. But savvy investors are quietly building wealth in Amarillo — a mid-size city on the Texas Panhandle that delivers strong rental yields, low entry costs, and a steady stream of motivated sellers. Whether you are brand new to the game or an experienced flipper looking for your next market, finding real estate deals in Amarillo TX is more accessible than you might think. If you are just getting started, bookmark our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in. It lays the groundwork for everything covered here.
Amarillo TX Real Estate Market Overview

Amarillo is the 14th largest city in Texas with a population hovering around 210,000 people. It sits at the crossroads of I-40 and I-27, making it a regional hub for trade, agriculture, and healthcare. The economy is anchored by the medical sector, agriculture, energy production, and a growing logistics industry. Unemployment consistently runs below the national average, and the city has attracted steady in-migration from smaller surrounding towns seeking better job access and healthcare.

The housing market here reflects the city's no-nonsense character. Prices are affordable, turnover is consistent, and there is no shortage of aging housing stock that creates opportunity for wholesalers and flippers alike. Average Home Prices in Amarillo TX

As of late 2024, the median home price in Amarillo sits around $215,000 — well below the Texas state median of roughly $295,000. Entry-level homes in investor-friendly zip codes can still be found in the $80,000 to $140,000 range, while move-in-ready properties in stronger neighborhoods typically land between $175,000 and $260,000. Luxury properties above $400,000 exist but represent a much smaller share of total sales volume. This price spread creates real opportunity for wholesalers who can lock up distressed properties at deep discounts and still deliver attractive margins to their buyers.

Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Amarillo
Not every zip code in Amarillo performs the same for investors. Understanding the local geography helps you target the right deals for your strategy.
South Amarillo (79109, 79118, 79119)

This is the most desirable residential corridor in the city. Home values are higher, schools are strong, and rental demand is driven by medical professionals working at BSA Health System and Baptist St. Anthony's Hospital. Buy-and-hold investors love this area for its low vacancy rates and quality tenant pool. Expect to pay more to get in, but cash flow is more predictable here.
Central Amarillo (79106, 79107)

Central Amarillo is the sweet spot for wholesalers and flippers. The housing stock is older — mostly 1940s through 1970s construction — which means motivated sellers are common, especially among estate sales and absentee owners. ARVs in stabilized blocks can reach $160,000 to $200,000 after renovation, while distressed acquisitions can still be found in the $55,000 to $90,000 range, leaving healthy room for assignment fees or flip profits.
North Amarillo (79107, 79108)

North Amarillo is a higher-risk, higher-reward zone. Prices are the lowest in the city, and landlords who know the area well can achieve gross rental yields above 12%. This is not a market for beginners operating without local boots on the ground, but experienced investors with strong property management can build portfolios here efficiently.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Amarillo TX
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is very active in Amarillo. The city has a large number of aging homeowners, inherited properties, and landlords who have grown tired of managing rental homes. Assignment fees in the $8,000 to $18,000 range are common on well-priced deals, and double closes can push those numbers higher on larger properties. To sharpen your approach, read our guide on [wholesaling real estate for beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) before sending your first offer.
Fix and Flip

Fix-and-flip activity has grown steadily in Amarillo over the past three years. Renovation costs in this market are meaningfully lower than in major Texas metros — experienced investors report all-in rehab costs of $20 to $35 per square foot for cosmetic-to-moderate renovations. A 1,400-square-foot home purchased for $90,000, renovated for $40,000, and sold at an ARV of $165,000 leaves a gross profit around $35,000 before carrying costs and commissions. Those margins are competitive by any standard.
Rental Properties

Amarillo's rental market is healthy and growing. Average rents for a 3-bedroom home range from $1,100 to $1,500 per month depending on location and condition. The city's large population of healthcare workers, students attending West Texas A&M University nearby, and blue-collar workers in energy and logistics creates consistent rental demand. Vacancy rates in well-managed properties typically run below 5%.

The best real estate markets are not always the ones making headlines. They are the ones where cash flow still makes sense and competition has not yet erased the margins. Amarillo is that kind of market right now.
Local Market Trends to Watch

items: Home prices in Amarillo have appreciated approximately 18% over the past three years, yet still remain well below Texas and national medians — suggesting room for continued growth.
Rising interest rates have slowed retail buyer demand, creating more opportunities for cash investors to negotiate favorable terms with motivated sellers.
New construction has been limited outside of South Amarillo, keeping pressure on resale and rental inventory in central and north neighborhoods.
The Amarillo National Center mixed-use development and ongoing downtown revitalization projects are improving the investment case for nearby residential properties.
Investor activity from out-of-state buyers — particularly from California and Colorado — has increased noticeably since 2022, attracted by lower price points and landlord-friendly Texas laws.

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals in Amarillo

The most profitable deals in Amarillo rarely hit the MLS. Distressed sellers, estate executors, and burned-out landlords often prefer a quick, quiet close over a full retail listing. Direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners and inherited properties are highly effective here. Driving for dollars in central zip codes still yields results. Tax delinquent lists, probate filings at the Potter County Courthouse, and code enforcement records are all valuable lead sources. For a deeper look at finding these hidden opportunities, our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) walks through each channel step by step.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

items: Build a local team first: Find a property manager, a contractor who will give honest rehab estimates, and a title company comfortable with wholesale transactions before you put a property under contract.
Visit the market at least once: Amarillo is affordable to fly into or drive through. A single day spent driving neighborhoods gives you context that no Zillow map can provide.
Understand the local insurance market: The Texas Panhandle sees hailstorms and high winds. Roof condition and insurance costs should factor into every deal analysis you run.

Use a deal analyzer before every offer: Run your numbers with the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to make sure your maximum allowable offer protects your margin.

Learn to analyze deals like a professional: Understanding repair estimates, ARV, and cap rates is non-negotiable in any market. Our guide on [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) will get you up to speed quickly.

Connect with the local REIA: The Amarillo Real Estate Investors Association meets monthly and is a great place to find buyers, partners, and local market intelligence from people doing deals on the ground right now.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When evaluating rental properties in Amarillo, target the 1% rule as a starting point — meaning monthly rent should be at least 1% of the total purchase price. In today's market, properties in central and north Amarillo can still hit this threshold, which is nearly impossible in most major Texas cities.
Is Amarillo TX Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Amarillo is not a flashy market. It does not have the tech-boom headlines of Austin or the population explosion of the DFW suburbs. What it does have is affordability, cash flow, consistent rental demand, and a motivated seller environment that rewards investors who do their homework. For wholesalers looking for assignable deals, flippers seeking manageable rehab numbers, and landlords building passive income portfolios, real estate deals in Amarillo TX offer a compelling case in 2024 and beyond.
